About Canoe Valley School

A developing secondary school for students ages 12–18 on a 40+ acre campus in rural Winneshiek County, tucked away in a tributary valley of Canoe Creek.

Our mission

Canoe Valley School aims to support students as they cultivate their whole selves and their connection to place, so they can find their path in life and proceed boldly, with creativity, care, and competency. Students, teachers, parents, and community members pursue this work together through self-directed, relational learning, and as a whole the school community aims to serve the place we live and help create a more beautiful, just, and abundant world.

We are a developing secondary school for students ages 12–18, rooted in the Canoe Creek watershed and the broader Decorah community. Our approach grows from a long local tradition of non-traditional education, while responding to a clear need for meaningful middle and high school options that are hands-on, place-based, rigorous, inclusive, and deeply human.

Our curriculum

The campus

The heart of our 40+ acre campus is an existing building that can be transformed into classrooms, gathering spaces, offices, and project rooms. Renovation will preserve the character of the place while making it safe, accessible, and ready for daily school life.

Canoe Valley is not imagined as a school building with a yard attached. The campus itself is part of the curriculum: a network of gardens, trails, gathering areas, farm spaces, and ecological study sites. Students will learn by moving through these places, noticing patterns, solving problems, and caring for the land that teaches them.

The school’s outdoor campus and planned educational farm are central to the learning we envision at Canoe Valley. We are developing spaces that support learning in ecological arts and regenerative farming, fostering development of hands-on, lived knowledge and connection to place.

The institution

The school is designed as an accredited secondary school serving students aged 12–18 in two multi-age groupings, a lower level and an upper level. It operates as a nonprofit organization with a multi-stakeholder board that includes equal representation for parents, teachers, students, and community members.

School leadership follows a teacher-administrator approach, with educators jointly sharing responsibility for academic, cultural, and operational life. Students participate meaningfully in school management and governance, including committee work connected to school operations and culture.

The school emphasizes partnership with other alternative-education institutions and allied organizations in the community and region, and serves as a hub and anchor institution for work of a similar spirit in the Canoe Creek Watershed, greater Decorah area, northeast Iowa, and the Driftless region. The institution is grounded in the school’s educational values, as well as institutional values like shared leadership and collective wisdom, relational agency, accessibility, and meaningful work.

Board members

Canoe Valley School is governed by a Board of local parents and educators.

Neil Martinsen-Burrell

Board President

Neil is a software engineer and former college professor. He has a PhD in Applied Mathematics and taught at Wartburg College before leaving academia for a career in technology. His family has lived in Iowa since 2006 and Decorah since 2013. He has three children ranging from elementary to college-aged and they have been homeschooled and attended Montessori, Waldorf, private, and public schools.

Nate Preus

Board Secretary

Nate grew up in Decorah, attended and was trained as a teacher at Luther College, taught secondary English at a public school in rural Wisconsin and at a charter school in Milwaukee. He then pursued a PhD in English at New York University, where he was also a part-time instructor, and later left academia to pursue another career path. Since his years at Luther, he has studied non-traditional education, and as a Fulbright grantee in the late 2000s he researched and published work on alternative pedagogy. He is the father of Ingrid.

Rachael Munn

Board Treasurer

Rachael grew up in Dubuque, Iowa and graduated from the University of Iowa with a degree in English. After several years of teaching English in China and Taiwan, Rachael returned to the University of Iowa where she earned a master’s degree in Special Education. Rachael taught at the secondary level for the Iowa City Community School District until 2022, when her family moved to Decorah to become the caretakers and project directors for ReRooted Connections. Rachael is a mentor at Red Oak Outdoor School and is passionate about gardening, local food systems, and outdoor education. She is the parent of Althea and Eleanor.

Kevan Klosterwill

Board Member

Kevan is a landscape designer and planner with Perez Planning + Design, where he focuses especially on public space master planning and visioning. Previous education experience includes teaching at the University of Virginia, during and after pursuing his PhD in the Constructed Environment there. He is the father of Alden and Gwendolyn.

Join our team

Our team is small, but mighty, and we have come a long way since those early conversations about what we want learning to look like in our community. However, we have some big steps ahead of us if we are to bring Canoe Valley School to life by fall of 2027, and we need help!

We are looking for team members who are able to donate 2–3 hours per week towards making Canoe Valley School a reality. Our next big endeavors include launching a capital fundraising campaign, increasing our enrollment commitments, and hiring teachers committed to Canoe Valley’s mission.

Canoe Valley School grew out of a village legacy, and we still need that village! If you have questions and/or are interested in joining the board, please reach out to info@canoevalley.org.
